title: Jordan Block Counts Without a Jordan Basis
content: The module docstring poses the open question inherited from the parent entry (cayley-hamilton-minpoly-oq-01-oq-01): how are the Jordan block counts per size recovered from the generalized-eigenspace dimension tower d_k(μ) = dim ker((f − μ)^k), without constructing a Jordan basis that Mathlib 4.26.0 lacks? The classical answer is Weyr's: blocks of size ≥ j number d_j − d_{j-1}, so blocks of exact size j number 2 d_j − d_{j-1} − d_{j+1}. For these to be genuine non-negative counts the tower must be concave, d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1}, which is the mathematical heart of the file and is proved with rank–nullity and submodule dimension calculus alone. Status: 0 sorries, 0 axioms; #print axioms lists only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
mathContext: For $N$ an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space (take $N = f - \mu\,\mathrm{id}$ per eigenvalue), the nullity tower $d_k = \dim\ker N^k$ is monotone and eventually constant. Weyr's characteristic $w_k = d_k - d_{k-1}$ counts Jordan blocks of size $\ge k$; the block count of exact size $k$ is $w_k - w_{k+1} = 2 d_k - d_{k-1} - d_{k+1} \ge 0$, the non-negativity being exactly concavity of $k \mapsto d_k$.

title: The Nullity Tower and Its Monotonicity
content: nullity N k = dim ker(N^k) packages the dimension tower abstractly, so it can be instantiated at N = f − μ•1 for each eigenvalue. ker_pow_mono proves the kernels of the powers form an increasing chain by the one-line argument: if N^a x = 0 then N^b x = N^{b−a}(N^a x) = 0 for b ≥ a (via pow_add and Module.End.mul_apply). Monotonicity of the dimensions (nullity_mono) is then finrank_mono of that inclusion, and nullity_zero (d_0 = 0) comes from N^0 = 1, ker(id) = ⊥, finrank ⊥ = 0. These are the FiniteDimensional-free structural facts the rest of the file rests on.
mathContext: The chain $\ker N \subseteq \ker N^2 \subseteq \cdots$ is the backbone of the Jordan structure: its successive quotients have dimensions $w_k = d_k - d_{k-1}$, and the eventual stabilization at $\ker N^{e}$ (the maximal generalized eigenspace) gives the largest block size $e$ studied in the parent entry.

title: One Level of the Tower as a Rank–Nullity Identity
content: jordanImage N k = N^k(ker N^{k+1}) is the image of the level-(k+1) kernel under N^k, a submodule of ker N whose dimension will turn out to be the number of blocks of size ≥ k+1. nullity_succ proves d_{k+1} = dim(jordanImage N k) + d_k by restricting N^k to the finite-dimensional subspace ker(N^{k+1}): finrank_range_add_finrank_ker gives dim(range) + dim(ker) = dim(ker N^{k+1}). The range is jordanImage N k (range_domRestrict), and the restricted kernel is ker(N^{k+1}) ⊓ ker(N^k) = ker(N^k) — computed through ker_comp, map_comap_subtype, finrank_map_subtype_eq, and inf_of_le_right using the tower inclusion. omega assembles the identity. This converts the abstract successive difference d_{k+1} − d_k into a concrete submodule dimension, with no Jordan basis.
mathContext: Restricting $N^k$ to $\ker N^{k+1}$ has image $N^k(\ker N^{k+1}) = \ker N \cap \mathrm{range}\,N^k$ and kernel $\ker N^k$, so rank–nullity reads $d_{k+1} = \dim N^k(\ker N^{k+1}) + d_k$. Thus $w_{k+1} = d_{k+1} - d_k = \dim N^k(\ker N^{k+1})$ is realized as an honest subspace dimension.

title: Concavity: the Block Counts Are Non-Negative
content: The decisive step. jordanImage_antitone shows N maps jordanImage N (k+1) into jordanImage N k: if v ∈ ker N^{k+2} then N^{k+1}v = N^k(Nv) with Nv ∈ ker N^{k+1}, so N^{k+1}v lands in N^k(ker N^{k+1}) = jordanImage N k (a membership chase via pow_succ and Module.End.mul_apply). Hence the image submodules form an antitone chain and their dimensions are non-increasing. nullity_concave then combines the two rank–nullity identities d_{k+1} = dim(jordanImage N k) + d_k and d_{k+2} = dim(jordanImage N (k+1)) + d_{k+1} with finrank_mono of the inclusion, and omega yields d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1}. This concavity is precisely the statement that the exact-size block counts 2 d_{k+1} − d_k − d_{k+2} are well-defined non-negative integers — the theorem that legitimizes reading Jordan structure off the tower.
mathContext: Since $\dim(\mathrm{jordanImage}\,N\,(k+1)) \le \dim(\mathrm{jordanImage}\,N\,k)$, the Weyr sequence $w_{k+1} \ge w_{k+2}$ is non-increasing, i.e. $d_{k+1} - d_k \ge d_{k+2} - d_{k+1}$. Equivalently $k \mapsto d_k$ is concave; the second difference $w_k - w_{k+1} = 2 d_k - d_{k-1} - d_{k+1}$ is the number of blocks of exact size $k$ and is therefore $\ge 0$.

title: Block-Count Functions and the Eigenvalue Interface
content: blocksAtLeast N j = d_j − d_{j-1} (the Weyr characteristic, blocks of size ≥ j) and blocksExact N j = blocksAtLeast N j − blocksAtLeast N (j+1) (blocks of exact size j) are read straight off the tower. blocksAtLeast_succ identifies the count with dim(jordanImage N k); blocksAtLeast_antitone is the size-monotonicity; sum_blocksAtLeast telescopes ∑_{j<m} blocksAtLeast N (j+1) = d_m (the algebraic multiplicity); blocksAtLeast_one gives the total block count = dim ker N (geometric multiplicity); blocksExact_succ_tower states #{size = k+1} = 2 d_{k+1} − d_k − d_{k+2} additively (no truncated subtraction). Finally nullity_sub_eq_finrank_genEigenspace uses genEigenspace_nat to identify the abstract tower of f − μ•1 with dim(genEigenspace f μ k), so eigenvalue_blocksAtLeast, eigenvalue_blocks_total, and genEigenspace_finrank_concave transport every formula and the concavity to each eigenvalue of f.
mathContext: With $d_k(\mu) = \dim\mathrm{genEigenspace}\,f\,\mu\,k$: the number of Jordan blocks for $\mu$ of size $\ge j$ is $d_j(\mu) - d_{j-1}(\mu)$, of exact size $j$ is $2 d_j(\mu) - d_{j-1}(\mu) - d_{j+1}(\mu)$, the total number of blocks is $d_1(\mu) = \dim\ker(f-\mu)$ (geometric multiplicity), and $\sum_j (d_j - d_{j-1}) = d_m$ recovers the algebraic multiplicity at the stabilization index.
